source.title: fileTypeFromMimeType misclassifies MIME types based on case and loose prefix matching

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
## Summary

`fileTypeFromMimeType` (`packages/workflow/src/utils.ts`) matches the whole Content-Type string with `startsWith`, which causes three classes of misclassification:

- Case sensitivity: MIME types are case-insensitive by spec, but `APPLICATION/JSON` and `Text/HTML` return `undefined`. One call site (`packages/cli/src/modules/instance-ai/eval/execution.service.ts`) lowercases the value manually while core and frontend call sites do not, so the same function behaves differently depending on the caller.
- Over-broad prefixes: unrelated types such as `application/json-patch+json`, `application/json5`, `application/pdfx` and `application/javascriptx` are reported as `json` / `pdf` / `text`.
- Parameters and surrounding whitespace are not normalized: `'  application/pdf ; charset=utf-8'` returns `undefined`.

## Minimal reproduction

```ts
fileTypeFromMimeType('APPLICATION/JSON');                  // undefined, expected 'json'
fileTypeFromMimeType('application/json-patch+json');       // 'json', expected undefined
fileTypeFromMimeType('  application/pdf ; charset=utf-8'); // undefined, expected 'pdf'
```

For comparison, `fileTypeFromMimeType('application/json')` returns `'json'`.

## Expected behavior

Normalize the media type to its essence (strip `;` parameters, trim, lowercase) before matching: exact equality for concrete types (`application/json`, `text/html`, `application/javascript`, `application/pdf`) and prefix matching for categories (`image/`, `audio/`, `video/`, `text/`). Valid inputs with parameters, whitespace or mixed case should be classified correctly; unrelated types sharing a prefix should no longer match; existing classifications for valid types should not change.

## Impact

HTTP / Webhook nodes use this helper to turn a response Content-Type into the binary `fileType`. Mixed-case or parameterized Content-Types (common in real responses) currently yield `undefined`, or JSON Patch / JSON5 payloads are mislabeled as `json`, so preview, download and display logic treat the file as the wrong type. The helper is shared by core, frontend and cli; the fix is confined to this single utility function and does not touch runtime core.
